text: The solver shows that a spacecraft could intercept the interstellar object 2I/Borisov by departing Earth on 2030-03-13, traveling for about 20 years, and arriving at the comet on 2050-03-13. The departure maneuver would require a C₃ of roughly 1727.89 km² s⁻² (the “departure C₃”) and would give the spacecraft a hyperbolic excess speed of about 41.56787 km s⁻¹ relative to Earth. Once it reaches the comet’s vicinity, the spacecraft would be moving at roughly 16.89188 km s⁻¹ relative to 2I/Borisov, which is the local encounter speed. The flight time works out to about 7305 days, or roughly 20 years, between launch and arrival. All of these numbers come from a patched‑conic, two‑body calculation that does not include any n‑body effects or non‑gravitational forces.
verification_status: computed with the same method; no published intercept study exists to validate against
